title: [Script] Make transpiler call helper keywords explicit
body:
The transpiler call helpers currently mix builder arguments and source-location metadata in variadic keyword dictionaries. Make the builder keyword mapping optional and explicit, with dedicated keyword-only parameters for `span`, `name_span`, and `value_span`.

Update callers to separate builder arguments from source ranges while preserving their evaluation order and leaving caller-owned mappings unchanged. This is a readability cleanup.

title: [REFACTOR][TVMScript] Fix syntax roots and simplify annotation scopes
body:
TVMScript selects special syntax from fixed dialect roots and reserved `range`/`int` names. Validate invalid bindings during prescan, then match direct `X.member` calls without reconstructing Python shadowing or following callable aliases.

Annotation helpers capture values under their original names so Python handles parameter, lambda, comprehension, and body scopes. Keep lazy symbolic-value adaptation separate from name lookup, preserve ordinary calls and symbolic range lowering, and use ordinary call contexts for nested namespace members.

Explicit symbols remove the need for unconditional-declaration tracking and expression-string namespace context. Remove unused module-decorator metadata and use the annotation read set directly while retaining lazy captures and source diagnostics.

title: [REFACTOR][Script] Separate builder protocols and concrete operations
body:
Move dialect builder implementations into their owning modules: package initializers expose exports, `ir.py` constructs concrete types and buffers, `op.py` provides expression operations and intrinsics, and `parser_protocol.py` owns function signatures, bindings, control-flow frames and statement emission.

Remove scalar and buffer proxy objects, migrate imperative callers to concrete loads and explicit indexed stores, and replace redundant capitalized control-flow wrappers with the parser protocol APIs. Preserve annotation syntax, native frame identity and exactly-once emission.

title: [REFACTOR][TVMScript] Simplify annotation symbol capture
body:
Depends on apache/tvm#20438.

Read explicit annotation symbols directly instead of wrapping each name in `require_defined` and `annotation_value_`. Snapshot the free definition bindings once, preserving lazy missing-name errors and separation from parameter and body scopes.

Remove captured runtime `typing.TypeVar` adaptation. Local generic symbols use PEP 695 headers with deferred whole annotations; external symbols use concrete `I.dynamic`/`T.dynamic` values. Keep annotation classes, Python unions, and deferred return-constructor normalization.

Bind a scalar parameter to an existing native symbol explicitly with `n: n`. An independently typed parameter such as `n: T.int32` shadows an outer symbol without an annotation-read registration side effect. Ordinary body locals may shadow definition captures; explicit header declarations retain symbolic reassignment diagnostics.

Global-info selectors use the builder resolver decorator after ordinary argument evaluation. Remove the obsolete parser argument-policy registry while retaining deferred whole annotations and concrete symbolic dimensions. The S-TIR namespace shares scalar annotation metadata and concrete dynamic constructors with TIRx.

title: [REFACTOR][TVMScript] Simplify annotation capture and transpiler contexts
body:
Simplify annotation construction around explicit function-header generics and concrete `I.dynamic` / `T.dynamic` values. Remove captured runtime `typing.TypeVar` adaptation, per-read annotation guards, and their obsolete bookkeeping while preserving definition-site scope, shadowing, and symbol identity.

Clarify shared transpiler inputs and generated body metadata, and capture definition values through original-name helper defaults while preserving lazy annotations, declaration timing, globals, and closures.

Resolve function construction through qualified definition-site decorators and preserve already-evaluated root options. Name fixed JIT arguments `const_args`, keep parameter construction helpers private to the transpiler, and document context consumers and helper contracts.

title: [REFACTOR][TVMScript] Align C++ builder and printer ownership
body:
Place TIRx, S-TIR, and Relax C++ builders under their `script/ir_builder` directories and flatten the shared IR builder directory, keeping parser completion beside its S-TIR builder consumer.

Move shared primitive-expression and literal/type handlers into the IR printer layer while preserving dialect repr/frame behavior. Keep PrinterConfig parsing dialect-neutral by forwarding extension keys and registering dialect-owned prefixes before name allocation. Consolidate shared shape printing and remove obsolete printer aliases and forwarding wrappers.

title: [Script] Introduce explicit dynamic symbols
body:
Introduce the shared `I.dynamic(name, dtype="int64")` / `T.dynamic` constructor for fresh primitive symbols that can be captured across script functions and modules. Replace `T.type_var` and implicit body symbol declarations with explicit captures or PEP 695 function parameters, including dtype bounds such as `def f[n, k: T.int32](...)`.

Remove parsing of quoted symbolic expressions in shapes, strides and offsets. These fields now use ordinary Python expressions over explicit symbols; whole quoted annotations and global-info selectors retain their existing roles. Update symbol printing and script callers to preserve dtype and shared versus independent identity, including the portable syntax for Python versions before 3.12.

title: [Fix][Relax][LLM] Synchronize merge_state_inplace before overwriting the LSE
body:
Add a barrier between reading and overwriting the shared log-sum-exp in `merge_state_inplace`, and
let one thread store it.

Every `threadIdx.x` thread of a block reads `S[bx, ty + by * bdy]`, derives both rescaling factors
from it, rescales its own `VEC_SIZE` columns of `V`, then writes the merged value back to that same
element. Nothing separates the read from the write, so this holds only while the threads advance in
lockstep. `bdx` is `head_dim // VEC_SIZE` with `VEC_SIZE` capped at 4, giving one warp per block at
head_dim 128, two at 256 and four at 512. Past one warp a thread that finishes early overwrites `S`
while another has yet to read it, and the late thread then rescales its slice of `V` with an already
merged LSE and stores an LSE merged twice.

The result is a large error rather than a rounding difference. On Metal at head_dim 512 with 8 heads
and identical inputs on every iteration, 22 of 25 runs at N=512 and 24 of 25 at N=4096 disagreed
with the first run, while head_dim 128 never did. Checked against a NumPy reference, one affected
row had 365 of its 512 columns wrong, confined to warp spans 0, 2 and 3, and the returned LSE was
off by 0.74. Gemma 4 E2B, whose head_dim is 512, hit this in roughly 3% of chunked prefills, moving
logits by up to 1.7 without changing the sampled tokens; a device sync after every VM call did not
remove it, which is what placed it inside a single kernel.

`merge_state_inplace_cpu` walks rows serially and is unaffected, and the measurements above are from
Metal, though the same argument applies to any backend whose blocks span more than one warp or
subgroup. The new case in `tests/python/relax/test_frontend_nn_llm_kernel_config.py` builds the
kernel for Metal and checks the generated source for a barrier between the last read of the LSE and
the first store to it, plus the single-thread guard; it fails at head_dim 128, 256 and 512 without
the fix.

title: [Fix][Relax][ONNX] Support Hardmax over a symbolic axis extent
body:
`Hardmax` is lowered to `argmax` followed by `one_hot`, but `relax.op.one_hot` takes its depth as a static integer attribute. When the reduced axis has a symbolic extent, the importer passed a `tir.Var` as the depth and failed with `TypeError: Mismatched type on argument #3 when calling relax.op.one_hot ... Expected int but got ir.Var`. For opset 12 and below the input is first flattened to 2-D, so the reduced extent is the product of the trailing dimensions and fails the same way (as a `prim.Mul`) whenever any of them is symbolic, for example `Hardmax(axis=1)` on an `[N, 3, W]` input.

This keeps the `one_hot` lowering whenever the extent is static, so the IR for existing models is unchanged. For a symbolic extent it compares the `keepdims` argmax index against an `arange` over the axis, broadcast along it, and casts the result to the input dtype. `argmax` returns the first maximum, so ties still resolve to the first index as the ONNX spec requires.

The tests cover opsets 11 and 13 with the reduced axis symbolic, a flattened extent that is a product involving a symbolic dim, a static axis on an otherwise symbolic input, and inputs with ties, all compared against onnxruntime. Six of the seven fail without this change; the remaining one checks the unchanged static-extent path.

title: [FIX][TIRx] Fix boolean bitwise-not codegen for C-like targets
body:
Fix incorrect code generation for boolean `BitwiseNot`.

For boolean values, bitwise NOT should flip `false` to `true` and `true` to `false`. The current C code generator emits `~value`, but C/C++ first converts the boolean to an integer:

- `~false` becomes `~0`, which is `-1`.
- `~true` becomes `~1`, which is `-2`.

Both results are nonzero, so converting them back to boolean produces `true` in both cases. CUDA boolean vectors have a related problem: their generated vector types do not support the `~` operator, causing compilation to fail.

This change emits `value == false` for boolean operands. It produces the correct result for scalar booleans and uses the existing vector comparison code to apply the operation to each lane. Integer operands continue to use `~value`..

title: [FIX][TIRx][CUDA] Reevaluate conditional wait predicates after each load
body:
Fix an infinite loop in CUDA codegen for `T.cuda.wait_until` predicates containing `T.if_then_else`. Previously, conditional temporaries were evaluated before the polling macro, so the predicate could keep testing a stale value after the destination was

  Keep statements generated for the predicate inside its repeated evaluation, preserving lazy branch semantics. Also correct the API documentation to describe load-before-test behavior.

  Add eight GPU regression cases covering signed/unsigned 32/64-bit words, with and without backoff. Tests run in isolated subprocesses with timeouts to contain hangs.

  Targets `v0.27.0`. Validated on TVM 0.27.0rc1 with CUDA 13.2 and B200:

  - Wait codegen tests: 25 passed.
  - Broader CUDA codegen tests: 202 passed, 4 environmental skips.
  - Downstream tirx-tools wait tests: 52 passed.
  - Compute Sanitizer synccheck and memcheck: 0 errors.
  - Scoped pre-commit checks and `git diff --check`: passed.

title: [REFACTOR][Script] Give S-TIR its own construction namespace

title: [REFACTOR][TVMScript] Resolve global-info arguments in builders
body:

title: [REFACTOR][TVMScript] Restore dialect-owned IR builder packages
body:

title: [TEST][Relax] Fix PyModule registry cleanup test after parser refactor
body:
After #20423 renamed the Python-function metadata to `__pyfuncs__`, the cleanup test added in #20417 still populated `pyfuncs`. Registration therefore returned early, allowing the test to pass without exercising cleanup.

This pr updates the fixture to use `__pyfuncs__` and assert that the function is registered before deleting the module. This ensures the test verifies that destruction removes the module’s own registration while preserving unrelated entries.

title: [FIX][Sym] Handle large masks in modular-set analysis
body:
Modular-set analysis constructs an int32 temporary for mask + 1 when checking bitwise AND expressions. Valid uint32 masks such as 2684354511 therefore raise a literal-range error.

The bug is already fixed in #20423, but that PR includes a large parser refactor and is too large to backport to v0.27.0. Port only the analyzer fix here: use an int64 temporary and guard the addition against signed overflow. Add regression coverage for the reported mask, large power-of-two-minus-one masks, and signed boundary cases.

title: [Backend][WebGPU] Fix off-by-one in the grid-packing guard
body:
`packGridDimX` is the number of workgroups requested along x, so valid packed ids are `[0, packGridDimX)`. The emitted guard only returned for `id > packGridDimX`, letting `id == packGridDimX` run.

The web runtime folds `blockIdx.x` into `blockIdx.z` to stay under the 65535 workgroups-per-dimension limit and pads x up when it is odd, so that id really is launched: for N = 100277 it dispatches (50139, 1, 2) = 100278 workgroups, and the extra one wrote `B[N]` past the end of an N-row buffer.

Fix: `>` → `>=`. The codegen test asserts the emitted guard; it fails on the current codegen and passes with this change.

title: [Fix][Relax] Scope BasePyModule's Python function registry entries to the module
body:
`BasePyModule.__del__` calls `vm.builtin.clear_py_func_registry`, which empties the process-wide registry rather than removing the module's own entries. Collecting any module therefore drops every registration in the process, and a later `R.call_py_func` fails with `Python function '<name>' not found in registry`.

Whether it happens depends on when the collector runs, so it shows up as an unrelated test failing. The module built in `tests/python/relax/test_pytorch_integration.py` registers nothing itself, but its finalizer wipes the names registered by `tests/python/relax/test_relax_operators.py`:

```python
tvm.get_global_func("vm.builtin.register_py_func")("victim", tvm.runtime.convert(lambda x: x))
bystander = BasePyModule.__new__(BasePyModule)   # registers nothing
del bystander
gc.collect()
tvm.get_global_func("vm.builtin.get_py_func")("victim")
# InternalError: Python function 'victim' not found in registry
```

This adds `vm.builtin.unregister_py_func` and records the names each module registers, so the finalizer removes only its own entries. Registering a name again transfers ownership to the newer module, which keeps a stale module from dropping a live one's function.

The per-module cleanup was also unreachable before this change. The wrapper stored in the registry captured `self`, so the registry held a strong reference to every module that registered a function and none of them were ever collected — the finalizer only ever ran for modules that had registered nothing, which are exactly the ones that then cleared everyone else's entries. The wrapper now holds a weak reference to its module, and reports a clear error if it is called after the module is gone:

```
RuntimeError: Python function 'f' belongs to a BasePyModule that has been destroyed;
keep the module alive while calling into it.
```

`vm.builtin.clear_py_func_registry` is left in place; it simply has no callers now.

title: [REFACTOR][TVMSCRIPT] Introduce a new transpiler based parser
body:
This PR introduces a modular, customizable parser infrastructure for TVMScript through transpilation. The key idea is to deterministically transpile language syntax into a corresponding sequence of builder calls while preserving source locations and providing span context.

Key design elements include:

- Acquire source and its definition scope, collect syntax facts once, rewrite the owned AST, and execute the resulting builder program with the original lexical bindings.
- Each language variant customizes behavior through a `parser_protocol.py` file, which defines special handling for syntax such as `for` and `if`.
- Create reusable span entries during rewriting. Attach locations to meaningful expressions and pass spans directly to builder operations that own them.
- Reuse existing builder and IR APIs, so new types and functions can be added without changing the parser, provided they have well-defined builder behavior.
- Generate specialization handling only when specialization is requested.

For example, this kernel:

```python
@T.prim_func
def add_one(A: T.Buffer((128,), "float32"), B: T.Buffer((16, 8), "float32")):
    for i in range(128):
        B[i // 8, i % 8] = A[i] + 1
```

is lowered to the following builder calls. This presentation wraps the emitted program in `build_add_one` and gives its local scaffolding readable aliases. `I` supplies shared builders, `T` is the language variant namespace, and `_S` holds source-span entries.

```python
def build_add_one():
    with I.IRBuilder() as builder:
        with T.function_(span=_S[6]) as fn:
            T.func_name('add_one')
            A = T.arg('A', _S[1](T.Buffer(_S[0]((128,)), 'float32')), span=_S[2])
            B = T.arg('B', _S[4](T.Buffer(_S[3]((16, 8)), 'float32')), span=_S[5])

            def build_body():
                A, B = fn.params
                with T.for_(T.range_(128), span=_S[7], names='i') as i:
                    T.setitem_(value=_S[9](_S[8](A[i]) + 1), target=B, key=(_S[10](i // 8), _S[11](i % 8)), span=_S[12])
            build_body()
    result = fn.function
    result.__name__ = 'add_one'
    T.check_well_formed_(result)
    return fn.function
```

title: [Web] Submit pending WebGPU commands every maxDispatchesPerFlush launches
body:
**Stacked on the unchanged-upload PR (#20429); only the last commit is this PR. Overlaps #19418, see below.**

Since #18871 commands are submitted only at flush points (sync, readback, host write). For a run of launches such as one LLM decode step the host therefore encodes everything first and the GPU starts afterwards, so encode time and GPU time add up instead of overlapping. On the GPU clock a Llama-3.2-1B decode step showed 2.0 ms of idle time between kernels per 5.4 ms.

Submit the pending commands once `maxDispatchesPerFlush` (default 32) launches have been recorded since the last submission; 0 turns periodic submission off. The field name and default follow #19418, which proposes the same knob for UI responsiveness.

Two differences from #19418:

1. A periodic submission must not restart the uniform pool. Every launch between two flush points keeps its own pool buffer at a stable position, which the bind group cache and the unchanged-upload check rely on; calling `flushCommands()` there took uploads from 13.9k to 50.7k per 256-token generation. So this adds `submitPendingCommands()` (finish + submit, keep the pool position) and has `flushCommands()` restart the pool even when nothing is pending, since a periodic submission may already have sent everything and any later `writeBuffer` is ordered after it.
2. `maxDispatchesPerFlush <= 0` there means "flush after every dispatch"; here `0` turns periodic submission off (the conventional meaning of 0 for an interval) and "after every dispatch" is spelled `1`. Happy to align either way.

Interval sweep on top of the three PRs below (1B, paired): never 1.000, 8: 1.101, 16: 1.107, 32: 1.110, 64: 1.091; uploads unchanged at every interval; text identical. Alone on `main` the mechanism gives 1.18×; the whole stack 1.28× (206.8 → 257.1 tok/s).

One invariant found by an independent review and now pinned by a test: `sync()` must still await the queue after a periodic submission that followed a readback, because the readback is no longer the queue tail (`pendingGPUToCPUCopyIsQueueTail` is cleared by the submission).

Tests: submission every N launches (default > 0) and a flush point restarting the count, `0` disables and the field is read at every launch, pool positions survive periodic submissions so caches still hit, the pool restarts at a flush point even with nothing pending, sync after readback + periodic submission, destroy-after-submit ordering. lint/tsc clean; jest 42 passed.

title: [Web] Skip WebGPU uniform uploads whose contents are unchanged
body:
**Stacked on the bind-group cache PR (#20428); only the last commit is this PR.**

Most kernels in a decode step receive the same POD arguments every token, and they land in the same pool buffer because a pool buffer is tied to the launch's position in the batch.

Remember the words last written to each pool buffer and skip `queue.writeBuffer` when the buffer already starts with the launch's words. Pool buffers are written only by `submitShader` and keep their contents across flushes. Comparison is on int32 bit patterns (exact for floats: `-0.0 != 0.0`, NaN equals itself). The pool keeps its own copy of the words, taken before the write and committed after it, so this composes with #18961 (one reused array per shader) and a throwing write leaves the contents unknown.

Uploads per token 199 → 54 on Llama-3.2-1B; the remainder are the arguments that really change (sequence positions, KV lengths).

title: [Web] Cache WebGPU bind groups of kernel launches in CacheState
body:
**Stacked on the compute-pass PR (#20427); only the last commit is this PR. Rebased onto `main` once that one lands.**

Follow-up to the review of #18871, which asked for bind group caching to live in `CacheState` with the key computation and invalidation spelled out. During LLM decode the memory planner hands each kernel the same buffers every token, so nearly every launch binds a combination that was bound before; creating a bind group is a round trip to the GPU process.

- **Key** (`CacheState.computeBindGroupKey`): an exact string, not a hash, so distinct bindings cannot collide: shader id (fixes the layout and the uniform binding size), ids of the bound buffers in binding order (buffer arguments are bound whole), id of the uniform pool buffer.
- **Ids** come from `CacheState.allocUid()` when a shader or `GPUBuffer` is created and are never reused. GPU pointers are not used because the buffer table recycles them after a free. Because the cache owns the id space, keys stay unique if several contexts share one `CacheState`.
- **Id storage**: a buffer's id lives at its pointer's index next to the `bufferTable` assignment, is cleared on free, and a launch asserts every id is defined, so a missing id can never alias two buffers in a key.
- **Invalidation**: none needed. Bind groups are immutable, and an entry is reachable only with the ids of the buffers it references, which stop occurring once one is destroyed. Dead entries hold no GPU memory and leave by LRU eviction. `dispose()` clears the cache.
- **Sizing**: the key includes the uniform pool buffer, which is tied to the launch's position in the batch, so the cache must hold one repeating unit of work (a decode step: ~184 launches for a 1B model, ~900 for 80 layers); below that every lookup misses and evicts. Default 2048, constructor argument.
- POD values are not in the key; they live in the uniform buffer's contents.

Tests: reuse across flushes, distinct buffers and shaders, recycled GPU pointer, defined ids in every key, replaced uniform pool buffer, LRU bound, two contexts sharing one `CacheState` and dispose. lint/tsc clean; jest 32 passed.

title: [Web] Share one compute pass across consecutive WebGPU dispatches
body:
The runtime batches dispatches into one command encoder (#18871) but still begins and ends a compute pass for every kernel launch. An LLM decode step is a few hundred launches.

This keeps the compute pass open on the pending encoder and reuses it for consecutive dispatches. The pass is ended before a GPU-to-GPU copy is recorded on the encoder and before the encoder is finished; every flush point already goes through `flushCommands()`.

Order and data dependencies are unchanged: WebGPU treats each dispatch inside a compute pass as its own usage scope, so a buffer written by one dispatch can be read by the next one in the same pass, exactly as with separate passes.

Tests: the mock device in `test_webgpu.js` now enforces the encoder lock (a copy, a second pass or `finish()` while a pass is open throws); new tests cover pass sharing across dispatches, every flush point ending the pass before the encoder is finished, and a launch that throws with the pass open. `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit` clean; jest `tests/node/test_webgpu.js` 25 passed.

title: [Relax][WebGPU] Sequence-sharded paged decode attention for long contexts
body:
The paged-KV decode kernel spends its threads across the head dimension (`bdx = D / 4`), so every q·k dot product is finished by a cross-thread allreduce, K/V are staged through workgroup memory, and one iteration of the serial loop over the context covers only `bdz * bdy` positions: 16 for a GQA model on WebGPU's 256 invocations. Decode attention is bound by memory latency per thread, so that loop dominates at long context. In a per-kernel GPU-timestamp profile of live WebLLM (Llama-3.2-1B, Apple M4 Max) attention is 10% of GPU time per token at 84 tokens of context, 50% at 1k and 75% at 3k, moving KV at ~13 GB/s while the q4 GEMVs reach 430.

## Change

A second thread nest for WebGPU (`_make_seq_sharded_decode_nest`), selected on the host from the page count (`nnz_pages > B * 256 / page_size`); the existing tiled nest becomes a `T.macro` and stays in charge of short contexts, where it is faster. Other targets are untouched (the generated PrimFunc is structurally identical for cuda/metal/vulkan/rocm/opencl).

- One workgroup per query head; the context is cut into up to 128 shards, each owned by `head_dim / 64` lanes (`threadIdx.y`), so a thread keeps 64 dims of q and of the running output in registers (2 × head_dim floats spills beyond 64 dims). Layouts: 128×1 for D=64, 128×2 for D=128, 64×4 for D=256, always 256 invocations or fewer.
- Per position, the lanes of a shard each form a partial dot product and exchange it through workgroup memory, double-buffered by position parity, so one `workgroupBarrier` per position suffices; the online-softmax state is updated per lane.
- Shard states are merged in two phases, (max, denom) first, then the weighted outputs a `CHUNK` of dims at a time summed one dim per thread, so everything fits the default 16 KiB of workgroup storage.
- A first version with fewer threads and no barriers was *slower* (0.63× at 3k): per-thread cost is memory latency, so throughput follows the number of threads in flight. Hence one workgroup per head.

## Measurements (Apple M4 Max, Chrome Canary, GPU timestamps)

Attention time per decode step at 3060 tokens of context, tiled → sharded: **2.90× / 4.00× / 3.45×** for head_dim 64 / 128 / 256 (Hq32/Hkv8 and Hq8/Hkv4 shapes, 16–32 layers; re-run on the final code). Break-even is at ~100–300 tokens for every head_dim, so the 256-token host switch holds.

End to end vs what WebLLM ships (npm bundle + prebuilt lib; this PR's libs also carry the GEMV config of the companion PR), decode tok/s:

| model | short prompt | after a ~2750-token prompt |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-q4f16_1 | 45.4 → 57.4 (1.29×) | 20.3 → 47.9 (**2.35×**) |
| Gemma-2-2b-it-q4f16_1 | 91.9 → 126.0 (1.37×) | 22.2 → 59.0 (**2.68×**) |
| Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-q4f16_1 | 200.7 → 279.4 (1.39×) | 83.8 → 167.4 (**2.00×**) |
| Qwen3-0.6B-q4f16_1 | 124.3 → 253.1 (2.02×) | 40.8 → 79.5 (1.95×) |

Generated text identical in every case (temperature 0). The short-prompt rows are the runtime + GEMV work; the long-prompt rows are where this kernel is selected.

## Correctness

Output and LSE match an f64 reference as well as the tiled kernel does (0.02% relative L2 = f16 output rounding, LSE within 2e-6) at nine context lengths from 1 to 3060 including odd shard lengths, with a shuffled page table; with `rotary_mode = 1`, sliding window and batch > 1 the two nests agree to ≤ 0.003% on identical inputs. Through the WebLLM API at ~2.7k tokens, top-5 logprobs shift by a mean 0.078 nat, the same as the floor between the prebuilt lib and a self-built upstream lib (0.070), with identical greedy text.

## Tests

`test_webgpu_decode_attention_dispatches_on_context_length` (two kernels, workgroup sizes, fewer barriers in the sharded one), `test_webgpu_decode_attention_lanes_follow_head_dim` (layouts for D = 128/256/96, workgroup storage ≤ 16 KiB), `test_decode_attention_unchanged_off_webgpu`. `tests/python/relax/test_frontend_nn_llm_kernel_config.py`: 22 passed. pre-commit clean.

## Open for reviewers

- Switch point (256 tokens) and shard count (128) tuned on one adapter.
- The same layout may help other latency-bound backends (Metal, Vulkan); not tried.

title: [Dlight][WebGPU] Add a WebGPU config to the GEMV inner-reduction schedule
body:
`dlight.gpu.GEMV` has target configs for cuda, metal, rocm, vulkan and two OpenCL variants. WebGPU falls through to the generic `else` (`TS, TR = 1, 64`), so a q4f16_1 decode GEMV runs one output row per 64-thread workgroup. This is what ships today: the decode matmuls in the prebuilt WebLLM Llama-3.2-1B lib (`binary-mlc-llm-libs`, `v0_2_84/base`) are all `@workgroup_size(64, 1, 1)`.

This adds a `webgpu` branch:

```python
VEC_C = 1; LOAD_V_SHARED = False; LOAD_V_VEC = -1; UNROLL = 64
TS, TR = (8, 16) if isinstance(len_S, int) else (1, 64)
```

## End to end (WebLLM 0.2.85, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-q4f16_1)

Two model libs built from source with MLC-LLM, identical except for this change (4 of 89 WGSL kernels differ: the four static decode GEMVs), loaded side by side, generations interleaved, 512 tokens × 7 rounds, Apple M4 Max, Chrome Canary:

| lib | decode tok/s |
|---|---|
| prebuilt `v0_2_84/base` (what ships) | 201.3 |
| built from source, upstream | 199.9 |
| built from source, this PR | **222.7** (1.11×) |

Temperature-0 output is identical across all three.

## Kernel level

GPU timestamp queries, every q4f16_1 GEMV of one decode step, kernels produced the way MLC-LLM produces them (fusion passes → `LowBatchGemvSpecialize` → production dlight rule order, `lm_head` with its symbolic `vocab_size`), one weight buffer per layer so each token streams the whole model:

| model | fallback | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | 11.67 ms GEMV / token | 9.28 ms | 1.26× |
| Llama-3.2-1B | 2.28 ms | 1.83 ms | 1.25× |

### Why (8, 16)

8B, ms per token over the (TS, TR) grid; `(1, 64)` is the fallback:

| | TR=8 | TR=16 | TR=32 | TR=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TS=1 | 24.18 | 12.71 | – | 11.69 |
| TS=2 | – | 9.38 | – | 11.73 |
| TS=4 | 9.68 | 9.44 | 11.95 | 11.86 |
| TS=8 | 9.65 | **9.29** | 11.82 | – |
| TS=16 | 9.85 | 9.64 | – | – |

The gain needs both `TR <= 16` and `TS >= 2`; neither helps alone. `(2, 16)`, `(4, 16)` and `(8, 16)` are within run-to-run spread; `TS = 8` also keeps `N / TS` under the 65535 workgroups-per-dimension limit for vocabulary-sized outputs. The 1B model gives the same ranking.

### Other constants

- `VEC_C = 1`: `VEC_C = 4` is within spread, and `CodeGenWebGPU` rejects vectors wider than 4 lanes.
- `UNROLL = 64`, not the 256 of cuda/metal/vulkan: at 256 the WGSL for 22016×4096 grows from 63 to 248 lines and is slower than the fallback.
- `LOAD_V_SHARED = False`: `True` fails an iter-affine-map divisibility check against the `// 8` nibble packing.
- `SUPPORT_WARP_SHUFFLE` is left at its default: it only sizes the shared-memory budget behind `LOAD_V_SHARED`, which is off here. Subgroup support on the target adds 1–2% on its own.
- **Symbolic `len_S` keeps `(1, 64)`, and this is required.** MLC's `lm_head` takes this path (symbolic `vocab_size`). With `TS > 1` on a symbolic extent the final store of the cross-thread reduction is emitted without the split predicate: for `vocab_size = 128257` the kernel writes 7 rows past the end. (That unguarded store is pre-existing and reachable today through the OpenCL Adreno config, which sets `TS, TR = 2, 32` unconditionally; not addressed here.)

## Correctness

Every kernel (all five shapes, both models, every config in the grid) checked against an f64 CPU reference with the output NaN-poisoned and guard slots after the last row: no NaNs, no writes past the end. Relative L2 vs f64 on the worst shape (14336 → 4096) goes 0.24% → 0.60% from the longer per-thread f16 accumulation chains (4-bit group quantization itself is ~9.5%). Through the WebLLM API, top-5 logprobs shift by a mean 0.016 nat at short context with identical greedy text.

Measured on one adapter (Apple M4 Max). `low_batch_gemv.py` was checked separately: its fallback is already the best config at batch 1–2 on this adapter, so it is left alone.

## Tests

`test_decode_gemv_webgpu` pins the scheduled TIR. `tests/python/s_tir/dlight/test_gpu_gemv.py`: 15 passed. pre-commit clean.

title: [Fix][Relax] Preserve symbolic shapes during constant folding
body:
## Motivation

For valid symbolic shapes, the `shape_to_tensor` fallback in `FoldConstant` can encounter a `PrimExpr` that is not an `IntImmNode`. Dereferencing it as an integer constant is unsafe. In the valid `shape_of -> shape_to_tensor -> tensor_to_shape -> reshape` path, reshape legalization also assumes a shape `Var` is bound directly to a `ShapeExpr`, but it may be bound to a call.

Related to #20260.

## Changes

- Fold `shape_to_tensor` through the C++ fallback only if each dimension is an int64 `IntImmNode` with a value representable as `int64_t`; otherwise retain the call.
- Preserve `reshape` when its target shape `Var` is not bound to a `ShapeExpr`, rather than asserting during legalization.
- Add regression tests for symbolic and mixed shapes, static folding through the fallback, and a valid dynamic reshape. The fallback tests temporarily remove and restore `FLegalize` to exercise the C++ path.

## Validation

- The complete `tests/python/relax/test_transform_fold_constant.py` file passes: 23 tests on the rebased source.
- The original valid dynamic-reshape reproducer completes `FoldConstant` without an exception.
- Both the `default` and `cpu_generic` LLVM/CPU pipelines build and execute with input lengths 3 and 7; outputs match the inputs.
- Pre-commit checks pass on the three changed files.

## Scope

Passing the Tensor result of `shape_to_tensor` directly to `reshape` without `tensor_to_shape` remains outside this change. In the BlockBuilder reproducer, that input is rejected before `FoldConstant` because `reshape` expects a Shape-typed operand. This PR does not relax that contract.

title: [WebGPU] Fix UI jank caused by compositor starvation in batched dispatch
body: Batching all dispatches into a single command buffer (introduced in #18871) blocks the browser compositor from interleaving its rendering work, causing visible frame drops and laggy scrolling during LLM inference. This adds a `maxDispatchesPerFlush` field (default 32) to `WebGPUContext` that flushes the encoder periodically, giving the compositor regular breathing room while preserving most of the batching throughput gains. Setting it to 0 restores the old per-dispatch behavior. Fixes #19342

title: [Fix][CUDA] Preserve NaNs in floating-point min and max
body:
### Bug: on `main`, the CUDA codegen prints bare `min()`/`max()` for `T.min`/`T.max` on float32/float16/bfloat16, so a NaN operand is dropped

With #20054's test data, the CUDA target gives 4/8 bitwise matches: the NaN lanes are discarded and the ±0 ties disagree with the C host.

### Fix

Same semantics as #20054: emit `(((a > b) || (a != a)) ? a : b)` for `max` (and the `<` form for `min`), so a NaN on either side is preserved and ties take `b`. Scalar form binds each operand once via SSA and references the temporaries; the vector form expands the same expression per lane. Covers float16/bfloat16/float32/float64. Integer and other non-float min/max keep the existing base-`CodeGenC` path, including the per-lane vector expansion. Only the CUDA codegen is touched; the host side is #20054's.

Generated source (scalar and per-lane vector), from the branch:

```
[float32/scalar] C_ptr[((int)threadIdx.x)] = (((v_ > v__1) || (v_ != v_)) ? v_ : v__1);
[float32/vec4]   __1.x = ((v_.x > v__1.x) || (v_.x != v_.x)) ? v_.x : v__1.x;
```

### Tests

Folded into `tests/python/codegen/test_target_codegen_cuda.py`: 4 dtypes (float32/float64/float16/bfloat16) × 2 ops × {scalar, vec4}, a composite case (`C[i] = max(A[i], B[i]) + 1.0` — catches the ternary being parsed as `(x + cond) ? va : vb`; NaN lanes assert NaN, finite lanes bitwise), and an int32 vec4 regression against numpy. Both compile paths (nvcc, nvrtc) are covered by the autouse fixture. Also `test_min_max_float_imm_operand_cuda` (constant NaN / non-NaN × lhs / rhs × min / max × scalar / vec4, once per compile path), with source assertions: the scalar constant fast path contains no `||`; a NaN lhs is the constant itself; a NaN rhs leaves only `(a != a)`; a non-NaN constant leaves a single ordered compare (reversed non-strict when the constant is on the right); the vec4 form takes the general per-lane path. A nested case, `max(0.0, B[i]) + 1.0`, is added too. The constant has to be written inline as `T.float32(c)`: a `c = T.float32(...)` statement in the prim_func body is a local buffer, and the earlier CI segfault was in the test prologue, not in the codegen.

A further defect surfaced in CI: the scalar path's SSA bindings stayed alive across statements. `SSAGetID` caches by printed text within the live scope and the base-codegen `BufferStore` dispatch does not invalidate it, so warp allreduce — which emits `red_buf[0] = max(red_buf[0], shuffle_down(...))` repeatedly — read the pre-write value from the second statement on: the first CI run had **92 failures in test_gpu_codegen_allreduce**, all finite values with max systematically too small. The scalar bindings are now scoped to the statement (`BeginScope`/`EndScope`, the same shape the vector path already had). A chained-statements test (`C[v] = max(C[v], A[v]); C[v] = max(C[v], B[v])`, `C` pre-filled) fails on the pre-fix code and passes with the fix.

Constant-operand fast paths (in response to tqchen's review on #20054): four cases — a constant NaN lhs is the result; a constant NaN rhs needs only the `(a != a)` test; a constant non-NaN lhs keeps the ordered compare; a constant non-NaN rhs reverses it to a non-strict one (`<` → `>=`, `>` → `<=`). A vector constant takes the general per-lane path.

### Verification

RTX A6000 (earlier rounds) and L40 (sm_89), CUDA 13.0.88:

- `-k min_max`: **74 passed** (nvcc + nvrtc);
- full `test_target_codegen_cuda.py`: **440 passed, 6 skipped**;
- allreduce suite: **328 passed, 330 skipped**;
- negative control (predicate forced to `return false`): **68 failed / 6 passed** — the 6 are the 4 int-vector and 2 chained cases, the latter green by construction since the control bypasses the new path;
- restored: **74/74**.
- `ruff@0.12.3` check/format and `clang-format 20.1.8 --dry-run --Werror` clean (per the run recorded in this thread).

NaN constants and NaN results are only guaranteed to be NaN, not a particular payload (on sm_89 nvcc normalizes some forms to `0x7FFFFFFF`); the tests assert `isnan` on the NaN lanes and bitwise equality on the finite lanes.

Partially addresses #19579 (CUDA side); host side is #20054.

title: [Topi] Support negative indices in topi.gather_nd
body:
Part of #20297 — this is the uncontroversial first slice (negative index normalization); the bounds-checking design for out-of-range indices is still under discussion on the issue.

`topi.gather_nd` passed index values through to the data access without any normalization, so an in-range negative index silently read out of bounds instead of counting from the end of the axis. `topi.scatter_elements` already normalizes negative indices (`k + (k < 0) * axis_range`), and the ONNX GatherND importer works around the gap by rewriting indices at import time (#20219) — but indices computed at runtime, or built through the relax API directly, still hit the raw path.

This normalizes in-range negative indices in the generated TIR, matching the ONNX GatherND semantics and the existing `scatter_elements` behavior. No changes for non-negative indices.

Testing:
- New `test_gather_nd_negative_indices_topi` covers `batch_dims=0` and `batch_dims=1` with indices spread over the full negative range of each axis, verified against the numpy reference (and it fails on unpatched main).
- The existing ONNX GatherND tests, including `test_gather_nd_negative_indices`, all pass unchanged (importer normalization composes fine with this).

title: [Fix][Relax][Torch] Respect zero-dimensional tensor dtype promotion
body:
## Problem

PyTorch dtype promotion depends on tensor rank. A zero-dimensional `float64` tensor added to a dimensioned `float32` tensor produces `float32`, but the Torch importer used `torch.promote_types` and incorrectly promoted the result to `float64`.

## Changes

- Use `torch.result_type` on meta tensors when both operand ranks are known.
- Preserve the existing `torch.promote_types` behavior for unknown ranks.
- Add regression coverage for both operand orders.

## Testing

title: [Fix][Sym] Use a typed zero for the sign test in interval Mul/Div
body:
When interval-set analysis combines a bounded interval with a single point of unknown sign in a `Mul` or `Div`, it builds `Select(b >= 0, ...)` to pick the bound order. The zero in that comparison was written as `IntImm(b->min_value.ty().WithLanes(1), 0)`, which aborts when `b` is a float expression:

```
Check failed: (value_ty.MatchesCode(kDLInt, kDLUInt, kDLBool)) is false:
IntImm supports only int or uint or bool type, but float32 was supplied.
```

Bounded float intervals come from casting an integer iterator, which is exactly what TOPI resize does when it computes `float(x) * (in / out)`. As a result, lowering a linear `resize2d` whose output size is a symbolic multiple of the input, such as `(2 * H, 3 * W)`, crashes in `LowerIntrin`:

```python
import tvm
from tvm import te, topi

H, W = tvm.tirx.Var("H", "int64"), tvm.tirx.Var("W", "int64")
x = te.placeholder((2, 3, H, W), "float32")
y = topi.image.resize2d(x, [0.0] * 4, (H * 2, W * 3), "NCHW", "linear", "asymmetric", "")
tvm.compile(tvm.IRModule({"main": te.create_prim_func([x, y])}), target="llvm")
```

The same crash is reachable at the analyzer level with `analyzer.int_set(float(i) * y, {i: [0, 4]})`. The fix builds the zero with `MakeConstScalar`, so it matches the operand type. For integer operands this produces the same `IntImm` as before, and for floats the branch previously always aborted, so no existing result changes. The `FloorDiv` site is integer-only and is updated only for consistency.

The new test checks the resulting `Mul` and `Div` bounds for positive and negative values of the unknown-sign operand. With the fix, the resize example above compiles and runs, and the `tests/python/sym` suite passes.

title: [Fix][Relax][VM] Stop BasePyModule from wiping the call_py_func registry
body:
`tests/python/relax/test_relax_operators.py::test_op_call_py_func` fails intermittently in CI with

```
tvm.error.InternalError: Python function 'torch_relu' not found in registry
```

(for example in the `cpu/pr-head` run of #20406, where it was the only failure out of 11,464 tests). The cause is `BasePyModule.__del__`, which clears the entire global `call_py_func` registry. `BasePyModule` instances sit in reference cycles, because the wrappers they attach capture `self`, so they are freed by the cyclic garbage collector at an arbitrary later point. When a module left over from an earlier test in the same pytest-xdist worker is collected between `register_py_func("torch_relu", ...)` and the VM call, the function the test just registered disappears. The same thing can happen to users: dropping any `BasePyModule` silently removes Python functions registered by unrelated code.

This reproduces deterministically:

```python
import gc, numpy as np, tvm
from tvm.relax.base_py_module import BasePyModule
from tvm.script import relax as R

@tvm.script.ir_module
class Mod:
    @R.function
    def main(x: R.Tensor((3,), "float32")):
        return R.call_py_func(R.str("f"), (x,), out_ty=R.Tensor((3,), "float32"))

vm = tvm.relax.VirtualMachine(tvm.compile(Mod, target="llvm"), tvm.cpu())
gc.disable()
BasePyModule(tvm.IRModule({}), device=tvm.cpu(0), target="llvm")
tvm.get_global_func("vm.builtin.register_py_func")("f", lambda x: x[0])
gc.collect()
vm["main"](tvm.runtime.tensor(np.zeros(3, "float32")))  # "Python function 'f' not found in registry"
```

The global clear cannot remove the module's own entries in any case, because the registered wrappers keep the module alive until they are removed. It appears to exist to avoid a crash at exit. The registry was a static `std::unordered_map`, and destroying it after the interpreter has been finalized releases the Python callables it holds. Any process that exits with a function still registered aborts with `double free or corruption` (exit code 134); this is reproducible with just `import tvm` and one `register_py_func` call.

This PR fixes both problems at the source. The registry becomes a heap-allocated singleton that is never destroyed, which is the usual way to avoid static destruction order issues, so nothing is released after finalization. `BasePyModule.__del__`, whose only job was the global clear, is removed.

The new tests check that collecting an unrelated `BasePyModule` keeps a registered function callable from the VM in both bytecode and compiled mode, and that a subprocess exiting with a function still registered returns 0. All three fail without this change. The existing `call_py_func`, `BasePyModule`, PyTorch integration and DLPack tests pass.

title: [Fix][Relax][ONNX] Fix Upsample and Resize-10 import
body:
The ONNX importer's handling of the legacy upsampling ops was broken in ways that affect most real models that use them. `Upsample` only exists in opsets 7 to 9 and `Resize-10` is its direct successor, so these are exactly the ops found in older exported models such as YOLOv3-era detectors.

For `Upsample-9`, `scales` became an input, but the converter still read the removed attribute, so every opset 9 model failed with `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`. For `Upsample-7/8` the model imported, but nearest mode was lowered with `resize2d`'s default `round` rounding. Upsample maps each output index to `floor(x_out / scale)`, so the imported model silently produced wrong values even for plain 2x upsampling (max abs diff around 4.8 against onnxruntime on random input). Every input dimension was also forced through `int()`, so a dynamic batch or spatial extent failed with `int(Var)`, and non-4-D inputs were rejected by bare asserts.

`Resize-10` has the signature `(X, scales)` and the same semantics as `Upsample-9`, but because only `_impl_v18` existed it was dispatched to the Resize-18 converter, which interpreted `scales` as `roi` and failed for every Resize-10 model.

This PR lowers `Upsample-7`, `Upsample-9` and `Resize-10` through one helper that follows the legacy semantics as implemented by onnxruntime. Output extents are `floor(input * scale)`, coordinates are asymmetric, and nearest mode rounds the source index down when upsampling and up when downsampling (Resize-10 accepts scales below one). Symbolic extents with integer scales are kept as exact products such as `2 * H`, so they still unify with other shapes, for example a skip connection concatenated after the upsample. 3-D and 5-D inputs go through `resize1d` and `resize3d`. Scaling the batch or channel dimension, or mixing upsampling and downsampling axes in nearest mode, raises `OpAttributeUnImplemented` instead of an assertion. `Resize-11` through `Resize-17` are explicitly mapped to the existing converter so their behaviour does not change.

The new tests compare against onnxruntime for all three op versions across nearest and linear modes, 3-D/4-D/5-D inputs, a non-integer scale, Resize-10 downsampling, and symbolic batch and spatial dimensions. 26 of the 28 fail without this change; the other two guard behaviour that was already correct.

Two related cases are not covered here. Linear mode with a non-integer scale where `input * scale` is not an integer still differs from onnxruntime, because TOPI derives the coordinate ratio from the output size rather than the given scale; that is the problem addressed for Resize by #19698. Linear mode with a symbolic extent and an integer scale hits a separate crash in the interval-set analysis, fixed in #20414.

title: [Fix][Relax][ONNX] Support symbolic dims in SAME auto_pad pooling
body:
The ONNX pool converter converted every input dimension to a Python `int` in order to resolve `auto_pad=SAME_UPPER/SAME_LOWER`, so `MaxPool`, `AveragePool` and `LpPool` failed with `TypeError: int() argument must be ... not 'Var'` whenever a spatial extent was symbolic. #20398 reports this for a dynamic-width `MaxPool` taken from PP-OCR.

The input extent is not actually needed in the reported case. Both SAME modes produce `ceil(input / stride)` outputs, so the total padding is `(ceil(in / s) - 1) * s + dilated_kernel - in`, which reduces to `dilated_kernel - 1` when the stride is 1. This PR computes the padding from that formula in a single helper, `Pool.get_same_pads`, which only reads an extent when the stride is greater than 1. A symbolic extent combined with a non-unit stride still cannot be expressed as a static padding attribute, so it now raises `OpAttributeUnImplemented` with a message naming the dimension, instead of the `TypeError`.

Replacing the separate max-pool and avg-pool code paths with one spec-following helper also corrects two silent issues. `MaxPool` with `SAME_LOWER` derived the output extent with `floor(in / stride)` where the spec requires `ceil`, which gave wrong padding whenever the extent was not divisible by the stride. `AveragePool` ignored `dilations` when resolving `auto_pad`.

Tests compare against onnxruntime for extents that are not divisible by the stride, and cover symbolic batch and width dimensions for all three ops (structurally, and numerically with a concrete input). The dilated case is checked structurally against the output shape given by ONNX shape inference, because onnxruntime ignores dilation when resolving `auto_pad` and returns a smaller output than the model's inferred shape. When the kernel is smaller than the stride the spec formula yields negative padding; the helper clamps it to zero, and this path has no onnxruntime comparison because onnxruntime rejects such models.

Fixes #20398

title: [Fix][Relax][ONNX] Import Resize with empty scales tensor and symbolic sizes
body:
Models exported from PyTorch with `F.interpolate(x, size=...)` currently fail to import through `from_onnx`, and the failure comes from how the Resize converter unpacks its optional inputs rather than from the resize itself. There are two separate triggers.

At opset 12 and below, the PyTorch exporter does not omit `roi` and `scales` when `sizes` is used; it passes them as empty constant tensors. The converter only treated a missing input as "not provided", so it saw both `scales` and `sizes` and failed the `Only one of scales and sizes can be provided in Resize` assertion. The ONNX spec treats an empty tensor here the same as an omitted input, so this PR maps zero-element constants to `None` before the check.

At opset 13 and above, when the model has a dynamic batch dimension, the exporter builds `sizes` as `Concat(Shape(x)[:2], [H_out, W_out])`. That reaches the converter as a `ShapeExpr` whose leading entries are symbolic, and `int(val.value)` raised `AttributeError: 'Var' object has no attribute 'value'`. Only the spatial entries are used, and `relax.op.image.resize2d/resize3d` already accept symbolic output extents, so the converter now keeps non-constant entries as `PrimExpr`s instead of forcing them to Python ints. As a side effect, resizing to another tensor's runtime height and width (sizes taken from a symbolic `Shape`) also imports.

A minimal reproduction:

```python
import io, torch, torch.nn.functional as F, onnx
from tvm.relax.frontend.onnx import from_onnx

class M(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x):
        return F.interpolate(x, size=(8, 8), mode="nearest")

for opset, dynamic_axes in [(11, {}), (13, {"x": {0: "N"}})]:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    torch.onnx.export(M(), torch.randn(1, 3, 4, 4), buf, opset_version=opset,
                      input_names=["x"], dynamic_axes=dynamic_axes, dynamo=False)
    from_onnx(onnx.load_from_string(buf.getvalue()))
# opset 11: AssertionError: Only one of scales and sizes can be provided in Resize.
# opset 13: AttributeError: 'Var' object has no attribute 'value'
```

The new tests cover the empty-`scales` pattern with static and symbolic batch, `sizes` computed from `Shape(x)` with a symbolic batch, and spatial sizes taken from a second input with symbolic height and width. Each checks the imported output shape and compares against onnxruntime; all four fail without this change. I also checked PyTorch exports of nearest and bilinear `F.interpolate` at opsets 11, 13 and 17 with batch sizes 1 and 3, which match onnxruntime to within 2.4e-7.

title: [TIRx] Reject boolean div and mod
body:
## Summary

- Reject boolean operands in TIRx `div` and `truncmod` before LLVM code generation.
- Add a regression test covering `bool / bool` and `bool % bool`.

This replaces the backend internal-check failure with a clear `TypeError` at TIRx node construction. Integer, unsigned-integer, and floating-point division remain supported; modulo remains limited to integer types, matching LLVM code generation.

Closes #20399

## Testing

- Built the matching local CPU library from this PR branch.
- Direct Python API checks: boolean `div` and `truncmod` raise `TypeError`; `int32` and `float32` division still constructs successfully.

title: [Fix][S-TIR] Add a block-aware ForceNarrowIndexToInt32
body: #20378 moved block iterator, access region, and match buffer rewriting into `s_tir::IndexDataTypeNormalizer`, so `tirx.transform.ForceNarrowIndexToInt32` only handles functions whose blocks have been lowered. Callers that narrow scheduled TIR, such as MLC's compilation pipeline, get tensorized blocks with int64 iterators and int32 domains, which later fail in `CompactBufferAllocation` with a `mismatched types. int64 vs. int32` error. Every q4f16_1 Metal build in MLC currently hits this. Add `s_tir.transform.ForceNarrowIndexToInt32` for functions that still contain blocks, sharing the narrowing rules with the TIRx pass and restoring the check on int64 block allocations. The TIRx pass now rejects S-TIR blocks instead of producing inconsistent IR, and the scan dispatch tests that narrow dispatched TIR use the new pass.

title: [do not merge] tvmscript printer v2
[TEST][ONNX] Declare captured symbolic shape variables explicitly
body: Use inline symbolic shapes in the Min/Max expected function signatures and explicit int64 variables for generated reduction, split, and tile dimensions. Preserve shared dimensions across input/output annotations and broadcast expressions.

title: [Fix][TOPI][WebGPU] Keep sort merge passes off blockIdx.z
body: #19900 moved the merge path axis of the GPU sort merge passes to `blockIdx.z` on every target. The WebGPU backend reserves `blockIdx.z` to extend `blockIdx.x` beyond 65535, so sort, argsort, and topk fail to compile for WebGPU whenever the input needs a merge pass. On WebGPU, fold the merge path and section axes into `blockIdx.x` and keep the batch on `blockIdx.y`; other targets keep the #19900 mapping. This also avoids the `blockIdx.y` overflow of the mapping before #19900, which produced wrong results for large batches (for example, a batch of 128 at size 151936).

title: [REFACTOR][TIR] Represent thread binding as a parallel-loop annotation
body:
Represent thread binding as a String annotation on parallel `For` loops, removing the dedicated field and loop-kind value. The ordinary TIRx constructor accepts annotations and exposes no binding-specific API; S-TIR constructs and interprets the thread tag.

Update scheduling, builders, printers and lowering to preserve the annotation until binding is consumed, and rebuild transient IterVars only where lower-level thread attributes require them. Distinguish ordinary CPU parallel execution from thread-bound execution while preserving serial, vectorized, unrolled and extent-one thread-scope behavior.

title: [REFACTOR][TIRx] Group buffer APIs and remove generic composition
body:
Group TIRx buffer variables, loads, and region constructors in `tirx/expr.h`, and consolidate buffer-related types and their registrations in `tirx/type.h` and its implementation. Preserve the shared core `TensorRegion` representation and existing buffer semantics.

title: [CUDA][BugFix] Guard tensor map enums by toolkit version
body:
CUDA tensor-map enum members are C++ identifiers, not preprocessor macros. The existing `#ifdef` checks therefore evaluated false even when CUDA 12.8+ `cuda.h` declared packed tensor-map data types and atomic 128-byte swizzle modes. This caused host validation to reject supported swizzles and to skip their packed/128-byte validation rules.

This change uses the existing `CUDA_VERSION >= 12080` availability contract consistently for every affected dtype and swizzle validation path. Older toolkits still compile without referencing the newer enum members.

Testing:
- `pre-commit run clang-format --files src/backend/cuda/runtime/cuda_device_api.cc`
- CUDA 13 build with `USE_NVSHMEM=ON`: `cmake --build build --parallel 16`
- Downstream TIRx GDN swizzle path: 10 correctness launches and 3 benchmark rounds passed

title: [TIRX] Represent buffers as typed variables
body:
This refactors TIRx buffers into ordinary `ir.Var` identities carrying an
immutable `BufferType`.

## Rationale

The old representation kept a standalone Buffer object, its logical metadata,
and a separate pointer-typed data Var. Generic Var substitution and
buffer-specific rebuilding could therefore let identity, metadata, and pointer
type drift apart. In this change, `BufferType` is the single source of the
logical contract and `buffer_data(buffer)` is the explicit physical-pointer
projection; `DeclBuffer` records a view's binding.

## Simplification

- Generic Var scoping, substitution, undefined-variable analysis, and identity
  maps now apply directly to buffers.
- The pointer type is derived from `BufferType`, so the physical pointer and
  buffer metadata cannot disagree.
- The common IR path no longer needs a second Buffer object, duplicate
  constructor state, or a parallel buffer-only substitution mechanism.
- Metadata-changing transforms create a fresh typed Var and bind it explicitly
  at the replacing `AllocBuffer` or `DeclBuffer`.

Physical-root tracking remains deliberately local to the passes whose
correctness depends on allocation ownership:

1. Storage liveness/reuse attributes alias accesses to the owning allocation.
2. Pointer vector-type inference and rewriting aggregate evidence at that root.
3. LowerTIRx cleanup projects aliases to the remapped physical allocation.
4. Thread-allreduce's deferred remapper replaces or removes the owning
   allocation.

Each is a plain pass-local `Map<Var, Var>` flattened when a `DeclBuffer` is
visited. Parameters, `buffer_map`, and `AllocBuffer` seed roots; an alias to an
unseen typed source is rejected rather than silently treated as a new root.
Simpler passes decode the one-step `buffer_data` projection locally.

## Migration guide

### C++

- Treat `BufferVar` as a checked view over an ordinary `Var`.
- Read logical metadata through `buffer->...`; use `buffer.var()` for identity.
- Use `buffer.data()` or `builtin::buffer_data()` only when a physical pointer
  expression is required.
- To change metadata, rebuild `BufferType`, create a fresh Var, and bind it at
  the replacement definition site.
- A transformed `DeclBuffer` replaces its superseded declaration consistently;
  it must not leave a stale declaration beside the new binding.

### Python

- Buffer constructors return `tvm.ir.Var`; `.ty` contains `BufferType`.
- Use `tvm.tirx.is_buffer_var(value)` for runtime discrimination.
- `tvm.tirx.Buffer` remains an import and annotation compatibility alias for
  `tvm.ir.Var`, so `isinstance(value, Buffer)` matches every Var.
- Importing `tvm.tirx` installs the legacy metadata properties on Var.
  Non-buffer Vars raise `AttributeError`; buffer `.dtype` keeps its historical
  `DataType` result.

## Behavior preservation

The behavior-preserving follow-up restores established LowerTIRx,
FlattenBuffer, BF16, alias-lifetime, and declaration-replacement behavior while
keeping ownership logic pass-local.

The final focused correction completes typed-buffer integration at structural
comparison, retyping, specialization, annotation, external-output, access
detection, projection lowering, printer, and target-codegen boundaries. It
also preserves the physical source handle type for declared aliases and
retains allocation-backed versus parameter-backed identity where lowering
requires that distinction.

## Validation

- Debug build with LLVM 18.1.8 and CUDA: passed.
- LowerIntrin, C address-generation, padded-vector LLVM, packed CUDA, raw
  pointer, and rank-0/rank-2 access-pointer regressions: **11 passed**.
- Coherent NumPy 2.3.5 reproduced both missed `PrimType` conversion
  boundaries; the corrected runtime-trace and minimal-LLVM files pass
  **8 tests**.
- Broader affected transform, C-host, runtime-trace, minimal-LLVM, and
  commit-3 regression suite: **467 passed, 8 xfailed, 1 xpassed**.
- Matched CUDA 13.1 validation asserted `nvrtcVersion() == 13.1` in the test
  process and loaded `libnvrtc.so.13.1.115`. After the representation-safe
  TensorMap `address_of` migration, the two complete CUDA-codegen files passed
  **376 tests** with **159 skipped**.
- Complete TIR and Relax specialization files: **12 passed**.
- Isolated schedule-state regression: **1 passed**.
- H200 paged-attention float32 prefill/decode nvcc regression: **1 passed**.
- Repository-pinned formatting, all pre-commit hooks, and `git diff --check`:
  passed.

title: [Fix][Relax] Allow callers to specify scan index-width budget
body: Add an optional `index_bits` argument to `DispatchSortScan` so pipelines that subsequently force indices to `int32` can generate compatible continuous GPU cumsum hierarchies. The hierarchy calculation can otherwise emit 64-bit thresholds that fail forced int32 narrowing, as seen in MLC's Metal compilation path. Existing callers retain the upstream defaults: 32 bits for WebGPU and 64 bits for other targets.

title: [Fix][Metal][WebGPU] Preserve variable bindings when resolving allocation bounds
body: Track primitive `Bind` expressions in a per-function analyzer so allocation bounds remain provable after common subexpression elimination. Continue rejecting extents whose only upper bound is the integer type limit.

title: [FIX][Vulkan] Avoid device API destruction during Windows DLL shutdown
body:
Keep the Windows Vulkan device API alive for the process lifetime, matching CUDADeviceAPI, so DLL teardown cannot call into partially shut-down drivers. Preserve the cleanup from #7997 on other platforms and add subprocess exit tests.

Fixes https://github.com/apache/tvm/issues/20396.

title: [TIRx][CUDA] Preserve kernel launch calls and add CUDA host source bundling
body:
Preserve kernel launch metadata through `tirx.call_ffi_kernel`. Ordinary host targets lower these calls through packed functions, while `cuda_host` emits direct CUDA launches with explicit diagnostics for unsupported launch modes.

Add `tvm.backend.cuda.export_cuda_host(mod)` to concatenate retained CUDA device source before its host wrappers into one translation unit. Existing CUDA device code generation stays unchanged; source generation, compilation and loading remain separate steps.

CUDA-host wrappers use tvm-ffi and CUDA libraries for streams, scoped device selection, tensor-map encoding and error handling. Tensor-map descriptors use aligned host storage and the device's by-value launch ABI. Unsupported TVM runtime services are diagnosed during code generation.

Tensor-map initialization uses `tirx.tensormap_encode_tiled` to retain the final descriptor dtype and fixed options in call attributes, with pointers and dimensions as runtime operands. CUDA-host codegen emits typed arrays and a direct driver call; ordinary hosts keep the existing packed encoder ABI.

title: [FIX][TIR] Fix fixed-point multiply legalization
body:
Handle runtime operands, zero-exponent scaling, and integer per-axis flags. Restrict the fast path to Q31.

Fixes apache/tvm#20340.
Fixes tile-ai/tilelang#3014.
Fixes tile-ai/tilelang#3003.
Fixes tile-ai/tilelang#3006.

title: [FIX][TIR] Conservatively analyze unsigned branch conditions
body:
Fixes https://github.com/apache/tvm/issues/20343.
Fixes https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/issues/3235.

 Unsigned branch conditions can crash block access-region analysis because the inequality solver constructs negative coefficients using unsigned variable types, raising `cannot make uint from negative value -1`.
Keep unsupported unsigned conditions unresolved and conservatively analyze both branches, while preserving independent signed bounds.
Add regression coverage for zero comparisons, high-bit thresholds, wraparound predicates, and mixed signed/unsigned conditions.

title: [FIX][TIRx] Avoid stale constraints from mutable memory predicates
body:
This pr fixes incorrect simplification of conditions that read mutable memory. An enclosing branch can currently cause `StmtSimplify` to remove a nested loop bound even when stores inside the branch or loop change the value being tested. Assertions can similarly cause later expressions to be folded incorrectly.

Only record pure branch and assertion predicates as analyzer facts, and exclude memory-dependent branch conditions from iteration predicates.

title: [Fix][Relax][Frontend][Torch] Compare shapes without `==` on symbolic dims in the reshape shortcut
body:
### Problem

`_reshape` skips an identity reshape with

```python
if current_shape is not None and list(current_shape) == list(dims):
    return x
```

On a symbolic dimension `==` builds a `PrimExpr` instead of answering, and Python then asks it for a truth value:

```text
ValueError: Cannot use and / or / not operator to Expr, hint: use tvm.tirx.all / tvm.tirx.any, ...
  File "python/tvm/relax/frontend/torch/base_fx_graph_translator.py", line 2559, in _reshape
  File "python/tvm/ir/expr.py", line 347, in __bool__
```

It only surfaces when the ranks match, because list equality compares lengths first — which is why `x.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)` on a rank-3 input imports and `x.reshape(x.shape[0], 0, x.shape[0])` raises:

| expression | input | torch | frontend on `main` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x.reshape(x.shape[0], 0, x.shape[0])` | `(batch, 0, 4)` | `(batch, 0, batch)` | `ValueError` |
| `x.reshape(0, x.shape[1], x.shape[1])` | `(0, batch, 4)` | `(0, batch, batch)` | `ValueError` |
| `x.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)` | `(batch, 0, 4)` | `(batch, 0)` | ok (rank differs) |

This is the "40 pre-existing `ValueError` cases" I reported as out of scope in #20255 — I had assumed they were below the frontend. They are this line.

### Fix

`_same_dims` compares dimension by dimension: static dims as integers, symbolic dims with `tvm_ffi.structural_equal`, a static-vs-symbolic pair as different. A genuine identity with a symbolic batch is still recognised (`x.reshape(x.shape[0], 2, 4)` on `(batch, 2, 4)` emits no reshape, asserted in the test). An expression written differently on the two sides (`s*2` vs `2*s`) is treated as different, which costs a no-op reshape and never a wrong shape.

### Verification

The reshape sweep from #20255 (938 `reshape`/`view`/`flatten`/`unflatten` targets over inputs mixing symbolic and zero dims, output shape compared with `torch.export`'s, symbol names canonicalised):

| | matched | mismatched | of which raising |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 892 | 46 | 40 |
| this PR | **932** | 6 | **0** |

Per-case diff: **no case fails with this change that did not fail before it; 40 repaired.** The 6 left are the sweep's own renderer printing `s*2` and `2*s` differently (verified in #20255's thread), not the frontend.

`test_frontend_from_exported_program.py` and `test_frontend_from_fx.py`: failure sets identical before and after apart from the new test. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (v0.12.3) clean.

### Test

`test_reshape_symbolic_target_same_rank` — the first row above builds and matches torch under a dynamic batch, and the identity case emits no reshape. Fails against the previous head with the `ValueError` above.

Independent of #20372–#20376 (branched from `main`). Touches the same `_reshape` as #20255 (merged), one line below it.

---

title: [REFACTOR][IR] Promote primitive bitwise and shift operations to nodes
body:
Primitive bitwise and shift expressions currently use generic intrinsic calls, requiring separate matching logic in analysis and lowering. This change introduces LShift, RShift, BitwiseAnd, BitwiseOr, BitwiseXor, and BitwiseNot nodes and migrates compiler consumers to typed operands. Public builders and operators retain their validation and constant-folding behavior.

The migration covers reflection and traversal, Python and TVMScript, symbolic analysis including Z3, Relax and TIR transforms, and C/LLVM/SPIR-V/WebGPU code generation. Existing tests receive representation-only updates.

title: [Metal] Add TVM_METAL_STORAGE_MODE opt-in for correctness at scale (#20157)
body:
## Summary

TVM's Metal runtime allocates every device buffer with
`MTLResourceStorageModePrivate`. On Apple Silicon at graph scale
(~11+ chained producer-consumer dispatches with certain fusion
patterns, tracked in #20157) this exposes a driver-level correctness
failure: outputs are silently wrong, `cosine(LLVM, Metal)` drops to
~0.75-0.95 on the repro.

Switching the allocation to `MTLResourceStorageModeShared` (unified
memory on UMA — same physical bytes, stronger cache-coherency
guarantees) closes the gate to numeric equivalence with LLVM.

Adds an env-flag opt-in so callers can select the storage mode
without a rebuild. Default remains `Private` for perf; this is a
correctness escape hatch, not a default change.

## Verification (macOS 15.5 / Apple M2 Max)

| Workload                       | `Private` (default) | `TVM_METAL_STORAGE_MODE=shared` |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------: | ------------------------------: |
| WaveNet-style Relax subgraph   |     cosine = 0.7556 |               **cosine = 1.000** |
| Synthetic N=11 (gated tanh×σ)  |     cosine = 0.9465 |               **cosine = 1.000** |
| Synthetic N=20                 |     cosine = 0.7064 |               **cosine = 1.000** |
| MobileNetV2 native Metal       |    argmax = 915 (✗) |     **argmax = 470, 5.3 ms warm** |

All match LLVM to fp32 noise (`max_delta ≤ 2e-5`).

## What this doesn't do

Not a root-cause fix. On UMA, `Private` and `Shared` refer to the same
physical memory; the difference is driver-side cache coherency. Twelve
TVM-side hypotheses were ruled out via C++ instrumentation before
converging on the storage-mode workaround: Relax memory reuse,
`KillAfterLastUse`, TIR storage rewrite, per-encoder barriers,
per-dispatch `waitUntilCompleted`, buffer zero-init, MSL codegen (MSL
is byte-identical between working and broken sizes). The bug survives
all software-side synchronization and shows up only under `Private`
mode, pointing at Metal driver behavior rather than TVM codegen.

## Suggested follow-ups

1. Benchmark `Shared` vs `Private` on representative GPU workloads to
   decide whether the macOS default should flip.
2. Consider promoting from env-flag to a target-level config option
   (`Target({"kind": "metal", "storage_mode": "shared"})`) once perf
   is characterized.
3. File a companion Apple Metal report with the reproducer for
   driver-side investigation.

title: [ONNX] Preserve integer Div constant-fold precision
body:
The Relax ONNX importer constant-folds binary operations through NumPy. For integer `Div`, `numpy.divide` promotes the operands to `float64`, so `int64` values above `2**53` lose low bits before the result is cast back to the integer dtype.

This change handles integer constant operands directly with integer quotient/remainder arithmetic. NumPy floor division is adjusted by one when signed operands have opposite signs and a non-zero remainder, preserving ONNX's truncation-toward-zero behavior without passing through floating point. Existing tensor and `PrimExpr` paths are unchanged.

The regression test covers values immediately above `2**53`, a negative large integer, and both signed truncation directions.

Fixes #20281

- `python -m ruff check python/tvm/relax/frontend/onnx/onnx_frontend.py tests/python/relax/test_frontend_onnx.py`
- `python -m ruff format --check python/tvm/relax/frontend/onnx/onnx_frontend.py tests/python/relax/test_frontend_onnx.py`

title: [ONNX] Fix initializer prefix stripping
body:
The Relax ONNX importer used `str.strip("onnx::")` when `keep_params_in_input=True`. Since `strip` treats its argument as a set of characters, initializer names that do not have the prefix can still lose leading or trailing `o`, `n`, `x`, or `:` characters. For example, `neck...` became `eck...`.

This change uses `str.removeprefix("onnx::")` so only the exact PyTorch-generated prefix is removed. The regression test covers both a prefixed initializer and an ordinary initializer beginning with `n`.

title: [Relax] Skip 1-D inputs in CombineParallelMatmul

## Motivation

`CombineParallelMatmul` assumes both operands have matrix dimensions when it concatenates RHS tensors and splits the combined output. Valid matmul expressions with a 1-D operand therefore crash the pass:

- A vector LHS produces a 1-D output, but the rewrite constructs `relax.split(axis=1)`.
- A vector RHS makes the batch-dimension loop use `rhs_dim - 2`, which underflows and leads to an out-of-bounds shape access.

## Changes

- Skip rewrite groups whose RHS rank is less than two.
- Skip rewrite groups whose shared LHS rank is less than two.
- Add regression tests for both vector-LHS and vector-RHS matmul branches, verifying that the pass leaves valid unsupported patterns unchanged.

title: [Fix][TIR] Check allocation size arithmetic instead of wrapping around
body:
Fixes #20269.

Since the BigInt migration the element count of a constant shape is formed exactly, but the sites that turn it into a bit or byte count still used unchecked 64-bit arithmetic, so a shape whose size does not fit wrapped around and was then used as if it were a real size. Add a checked helper to `tirx/transform/ir_utils.h` that forms the whole product exactly and reports when it does not fit in `uint64_t`, and route the reported sites through it.

- `LowerTVMBuiltin` folds the byte count into the `uint64` argument of `TVMBackendAllocWorkspace`; constant folding wraps it modulo `2**64`, so the shapes in the report request 0 bytes, or `2**62` instead of `5 * 2**62`. The stack-allocation check multiplied the element count by the element size in `size_t` in the same way. A constant size that does not fit is now rejected instead of emitted wrapped. A shape with symbolic extents still builds the multiplication chain and is unchanged; guarding that needs a runtime check in the generated code.
- `StoragePlanRewriter::FindAlloc` multiplied the element count by the element bits in `uint64`. A wrapped product can look like a small known size, so a buffer is placed in an allocation far too small for it: `8 * (2**61 + 128)` wraps to 1024 bits, and the planner put that buffer inside a 128-byte one. A constant size that does not fit is now rejected, the same way `LowerTVMBuiltin` rejects it. Leaving it unplanned instead would make the tagged-memory path fail later on the unrelated `Special tagged memory must be const size` check. The `const_nbits * match_range` end of the free-list search is saturated: wrapping put the upper bound below the lower one, and the search then ran past the end of `const_free_map_`.
- The inplace check in the same pass compared the same wrapped product against the source entry, and no longer matches when the size does not fit.
- `VerifyGPUCode` converted the exact element count to `int64_t`, which now throws `OverflowError` from inside the analysis instead of reporting a violation, and then multiplied by the element bytes in `size_t`: a shared buffer of `2**31 x 2**31` float32 wraps to zero, and the kernel is accepted. The size is now reported as an error, and the per-block totals accumulate without wrapping.
- `MergeSharedMemoryAllocations` had its own copy of the element-count product followed by the same unchecked multiply. It now uses the shared helper and rejects a size that does not fit, and its search range is saturated the same way.

`AllocBuffer::ConstantAllocationSize()` is not touched: it already reports an element count that does not fit, but the callers need the size in bits or bytes, and that is where the remaining overflow was.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, CPU-only build with LLVM 18 (no CUDA), on `850a9d8`:

- New tests on the unpatched tree: `test_workspace_size_that_does_not_fit_is_rejected` (3 shapes) and `test_allocation_size_that_does_not_fit_is_rejected` fail with the wrapped size accepted, `test_shared_memory_size_that_does_not_fit[int8]` fails with `BigInt does not fit int64_t` raised from the analysis, and the float32 case is accepted; this is the report reproduced. The within-limit cases pass. With the fix all 10 pass. `test_reuse_search_range_does_not_wrap` also passes before the fix: with libstdc++, incrementing `end()` happens to land on the only free entry, so it guards the invariant rather than reproducing a crash.
- `tests/python/tirx-transform/`: 340 passed, 8 xfailed, 1 xpassed. `tests/python/s_tir/transform/`: 268 passed, 8 skipped. `tests/python/s_tir/analysis/`: 92 passed. `tests/python/s_tir/meta_schedule/test_meta_schedule_postproc_verify_gpu_code.py`: 8 passed.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. No GPU tests were run.
